Rows 2 (D-WORKFLOW-102), 4 (D-CLOUD-158) and 8 (P0) were superseded before writing.

1. **D-WORKFLOW-085 (refine):** upstream-owned paths and package names are retained while the fork tracks upstream; every new fork-owned artifact takes the `rasteratops` prefix from creation; the code-level rename is reconsidered only on a trial-merge cost report and is re-opened automatically whenever the pin-versus-track trigger fires.
2. **D-WORKFLOW-083 (refine):** the RetroArch-under-ES Step 0 spike may proceed on a branch before Tier 1 closes; merging it and releasing 0.1 require closure of Tier 1 punch items for the launch, control and state slice and of any known security, state-preservation or launch-path finding regardless of tier; Tiers 2 and 3 close before 0.2 and 0.3, except the Tier 3 launch-path slice, which gates #336 Step 1; this row takes effect only on explicit owner approval, otherwise the prior gate stands.
3. **Merge cadence and pin-versus-track (new):** upstream is reviewed at the owner-set interval with a security fast path and no merges during release qualification; every merge records upstream-owned diff size, patch-refresh effort and ES conflict cost separately, and imported workflows, scripts and patches are diffed before execution; when merge cost exceeds the pre-declared budget on two consecutive cadences, or two cadences are skipped, or a pin is decided, the pin-versus-track decision and the code-level rename are re-opened together.

5. **Update-channel trust assumption (new):** for 0.0.1 the update channel is authenticated by TLS to the release host plus owner control of the publishing organisation; the `.sha256` beside each asset detects corruption and does not authenticate origin; image signing is a designed slot for 0.0.x and is not implemented in 0.0.1.
6. **Runner trust boundary (new):** self-hosted runners execute only `push` on protected refs and `workflow_dispatch`, never `pull_request`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` checkouts of untrusted code; the runner user holds no persistent publishing credentials, no `sudo`, no Docker-socket access, and cannot read the bot, mail or signing stores; build, bot and owner are the only credential-holding roles; if any boundary cannot be enforced the runner stays disabled; credential revocation and security changes are exempt from any WIP freeze and are recorded when taken.
7. **Release publication discipline (new):** no CI image is ever attached to a Release; candidates live in the immutable candidate store keyed by digest and QA reads only from it; releases begin as drafts, use a pre-release for rehearsal only when the P0 read shows fielded clients ignore pre-releases, and become full releases only at the owner's per-release publication yes; under Branch A a device asset is attached only after that device's smoke test is recorded; if the owner is unavailable the release stops at the immutable candidate.
8. **D-WORKFLOW-088 and Choice 2 (resolve):** D-WORKFLOW-088 is cited from the register (the run's packet omitted it) and Choice 2 is labelled or struck before any dependent decision is finalised.
9. **Corresponding source and component inventory (new):** every published release carries a component-level inventory of shipped works with licence and disposition and preserves in fork-owned, backed-up storage the exact fetched source tarballs, patches and build scripts for every component whose licence requires corresponding source; public repository visibility alone does not close the obligation.
10. **Organisation recovery and 2FA custody (new):** organisation recovery must not depend on a second personal account of the same person or on authenticators that share one physical device with the bot secret; the remedy is a trusted second human owner or a documented reliance on the platform's recovery process, with a 2FA custody record kept off-host.
11. **Redirect sunset (new):** the fork stops depending on the old-name repository redirect once every fielded device has completed one fork-to-fork update; until then each release records the dependency; container namespaces and third-party embeds are not covered by the redirect and are re-pointed in P1.
12. **Identity default (new):** in 0.0.1 every persisted path, partition label, hostname, share name, mount point, unit name and machine-readable identifier keeps its RC2 value; only consumers the P0 sweep classifies as display text change; `DISTRO=ROCKNIX` and `distributions/ROCKNIX/` are retained; relabelling belongs to a later clean-install-only release whose init accepts both labels.
13. **Support matrix (new):** the matrix distinguishes build target, physical board and QA guest and records per target the clean-install result, upgrade result, boot medium and boot-chain deltas, recovery method and attachment status; a target with any boot-chain delta from RC2 receives its smoke test before its asset is attached, regardless of adoption branch.
14. **Backup scope and recovery drill (new):** non-reconstructible state is snapshotted off-host with a recorded snapshot ID and a verified representative restore; credential recovery material is separately encrypted under owner control; the secret-free, role-specific blueprint reproduces toolchain and worktrees on a clean host, no build or QA host receives control-account credentials, and provisioning the second host is the restore drill.
